title: How We Know
subtitle: Source · text · stone · witness · experiment · argument · tradition · limit

charter.title: Name the evidence
charter.text: Every claim begins by identifying what was actually observed, measured, read, recovered, or reported.

charter.title: Show the bridge
charter.text: The move from evidence to explanation is written out. An inference never masquerades as an observation.

charter.title: Keep rivals visible
charter.text: Serious alternative explanations remain beside the preferred interpretation instead of disappearing from the page.

charter.title: State the limit
charter.text: Every case ends with what its evidence cannot establish. The boundary is part of the finding.

layers.label: Observed
layers.question: What is actually there?
layers.text: Measurements, experiments, texts, artifacts, testimony, and documented events—kept in their own evidence class.

layers.label: Inferred
layers.question: What follows from it?
layers.text: Historical, scientific, and philosophical reasoning, with assumptions and competing explanations exposed.

layers.label: Interpreted
layers.question: What does it mean?
layers.text: A theological, philosophical, or communal reading, identified as a reading rather than relabeled as raw data.

rooms.label: Source
rooms.question: Where did it come from?
rooms.text: Identify the maker, date, purpose, custody, translation, and distance from the event before using a record.
rooms.example: The site-wide source map keeps provenance beside every world.

rooms.label: Text
rooms.question: What do the words support?
rooms.text: Read wording, genre, language, manuscript transmission, and context before building a claim on a passage.
rooms.example: The hosted reader exposes the actual text and canon boundary.

rooms.label: Stone
rooms.question: What survives materially?
rooms.text: Artifacts can establish people, places, offices, practices, and settings without silently inheriting every literary claim around them.
rooms.example: The Jesus history room places each object beside its limit.

rooms.label: Witness
rooms.question: Who says so, and when?
rooms.text: Test proximity, independence, interest, agreement, conflict, and silence before treating testimony as corroboration.
rooms.example: The apostles' roads separate Scripture, early sources, and later tradition.

rooms.label: Experiment
rooms.question: What can be measured again?
rooms.text: Ask what was measured, how uncertainty was handled, and whether a result is repeatable, reproducible, or singular.
rooms.example: The Faith & Science docket begins with method, not a desired conclusion.

rooms.label: Argument
rooms.question: Does the conclusion follow?
rooms.text: Expose assumptions, inferential steps, rival explanations, and the difference between possibility, probability, and proof.
rooms.example: Every Claim Lab card makes the bridge from record to conclusion visible.

rooms.label: Tradition
rooms.question: What was handed on?
rooms.text: Track how communities receive, preserve, interpret, develop, or dispute a claim without backdating later consensus.
rooms.example: The early writings show transmission and reception without erasing canon boundaries.

rooms.label: Limit
rooms.question: What does this not prove?
rooms.text: A conclusion earns trust by naming the nearest claim the evidence cannot carry and by refusing to cross that line.
rooms.example: The Angels room distinguishes a passage's named subject from later theological readings.

claimLab.title: The Pilate Stone
claimLab.question: What does the Pilate Stone establish?
claimLab.record: The damaged Latin inscription securely preserves Pilate's name and the title “prefect of Judaea.”
claimLab.inference: It anchors Pontius Pilate and his office in the material record and lets the title be checked against literary witnesses.
claimLab.limit: It does not mention Jesus or a trial, and restorations outside the secure name and title remain debated.

claimLab.title: Where the apostles went
claimLab.question: When does a mission tradition become historical evidence?
claimLab.record: The Apostles world labels what the New Testament states, what early sources add, and what appears only in later tradition.
claimLab.inference: A route or death claim grows stronger when it is earlier, independent, specific, and close to the people or events described.
claimLab.limit: A detailed late retelling does not become an early witness merely because later communities repeat it.

claimLab.title: A text survives
claimLab.question: What can manuscript survival tell us?
claimLab.record: Each hosted early writing names its date range, translation source, and survival notes when the data supplies them.
claimLab.inference: Manuscripts and reception history can show that a work circulated, where it was read, and how communities treated it.
claimLab.limit: Survival, copying, or local reception does not by itself establish apostolic authorship or universal canon status.

claimLab.title: The fall behind the taunt
claimLab.question: Do Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 narrate Satan's fall?
claimLab.record: Isaiah's taunt names the king of Babylon; Ezekiel's lament names the king of Tyre. Both use imagery the church later read as echoing an older fall.
claimLab.inference: Immediate literary context and later theological reception can be shown together without pretending they are the same layer.
claimLab.limit: The two passages alone do not supply a complete biography of Satan; the second referent is an interpretation.

claimLab.title: The legal fence
claimLab.question: What can an ownership record settle?
claimLab.record: Rights-holder policies, licenses, publisher notices, and court records document control claims and permitted uses.
claimLab.inference: Those records can establish a legal status, practical restriction, or judicial outcome in a particular place and time.
claimLab.limit: Legal control does not decide theological legitimacy, spiritual authority, or whether a restriction is wise.

claimLab.title: A council decides
claimLab.question: What does a council record establish?
claimLab.record: The council room places date, caller, decision, primary text, and historical consequence beside one another.
claimLab.inference: Comparing a decree with its later reception shows how an institutional judgment entered doctrine and practice.
claimLab.limit: The decree establishes what a body decided; it does not by itself establish universal reception or divine truth.

claimLab.title: The post-mortem horizon
claimLab.question: What can comparative afterlife frameworks establish?
claimLab.record: 54 world traditions preserve funerary archaeology, burial inscriptions, and sacred texts describing realms beyond death.
claimLab.inference: Comparative analysis isolates recurring structural motifs (moral judgment, chthonic gates, soul ascent) across independent cultures and eras.
claimLab.limit: The historical and textual record establishes what human cultures believed, buried, and wrote; it cannot verify the empirical reality of the post-mortem state.

faithScience.title: Faith & Science
faithScience.lede: A secondary investigation lane for questions that cross scientific, philosophical, historical, and theological domains.
faithScience.principle: Science can constrain a theological claim, create a question theology may interpret, or expose a bad analogy. It cannot be made to confess a doctrine its methods do not measure.

docket.title: The Big Bang and creation
docket.question: Does an early hot, expanding universe equal creation from nothing?
docket.boundary: A physical history is not yet a metaphysical origin.

docket.title: Fine-tuning
docket.question: What is measured, and where do design or multiverse arguments begin?
docket.boundary: The data does not choose its own explanation.

docket.title: Evolution and providence
docket.question: How can an unfolding creation relate to purpose and divine action?
docket.boundary: A biological mechanism is not a complete theology of creation.

docket.title: Consciousness and the soul
docket.question: What can neuroscience measure, and what remains philosophical?
docket.boundary: Neural dependence does not by itself settle personal identity or soul.

docket.title: Miracles and resurrection
docket.question: Which parts are scientific, historical, and theological questions?
docket.boundary: A repeatable method cannot replay a claimed singular event.

docket.title: The Trinity and creation
docket.question: What may creation echo, and what only revelation supplies?
docket.boundary: Resonance is not demonstration; a recurring three is not evidence of three divine persons.
